column5: Overall Review of Roblox from a Users Standpoint
column6: I started playing this game in 2009 and to this day, I haven't seen many problems. Sure there are "violent" or "innapropriate" games, but that really depends on your household standards. Say, if a strict household were to see their child playing Assasin or Jailbreak, then there you have it. A bad review. But if a less strict household were to see their child play the same games, then boom. No bad review. Even when I was 10 years old, I never experienced any child predators of any sort. The parents concerned about this should just monitor their child closely. Roblox is rated 12+ on Google Play and Apple, so by then, your child should be old enough to know about the bad things and the things that they should not do. Roblox was smart in rating it 12+, because by that age most people know what to do if a person or thing that is not appropriate shows up. Aside from it's few flaws, it is truly hard now days to create an MMO (Massively Multiplayer Online) game that is targeted towards an audience of kids. For any parents out there, I reccomend you check out Roblox first and see if it fits with the standards of your own individual household. Now let's talk about money. As I said in the MMO game statement, in order to maintain a game of this scale, the company needs money. Although in-game currency cost a lot, and the conversion to real money is really unstable, the player does not need a lot of money to make themselves look cool. To do this, Roblox added in a way of people uploading their own designs that they can sell for their own Robux. Roblox heavily moderates the designs, and I have never seen an innapropriate product in my life. Roblox also recently added a Robux conversion for those Developers who earn a lot of Robux, to get changed into real money. The last section I will be talking about is the developing stage. To maintain a steady flow of users and community members, Roblox allows for users to create games using Roblox Studio. Using different tools that include coding, the player can create what he/she wants to create. Like the designs, Roblox heavily moderates these games, and if innapropriate content is found , then the game is put under review and closed to the public. My final verdict, is yes. I do believe that Roblox is a good game for those 12 and older. But under that age, uneducated kids might run into some problems.

column6: This is coming from the experience of somebody who has been on the platform since 2016 and is now 16 years old: if your child is under 13, disable the ability to make friends or chat. Also, register your child’s account in your email and password  and don’t tell your child that email/password; this way they won’t fall for scams that will steal their account and if your child does try to make edits to parental settings, it will notify you. Another thing is make sure the age is set up accurately, you have the ability to voice chat if you can verify that you’re over 15 at the least and there is no moderation with voice chat, it is also extremely easy to fake your age. Other than that the platform is extremely fun and engaging and functions much like YouTube,  just for player-made games. Your child can learn coding and game design as well as being able to publish those games and play other games, not to mention how you can learn how to create UCG items that can be bought and sold within game (this takes experience, but can be very worthwhile and IICR you can make actual money). Also, if you are going to buy your child robux (in-game currency) do not get the monthly subscription, buy independently and when your child actually wants something specific (an outfit item, gamepass, etc) Highly recommend!

column6:
Roblox is a fun and resourceful game, kids can learn about scripting, which may come into play in the future (The coding language/type is LUA, a simple starter) And games are made as family friendly as possible. Although some games have content inappropriate for younger players, to disable this click the three dots on the top right corner of the screen and go to Settings --> Security and then click on "Account Restrictions" If you don't feel safe with your child contacting other users, go to Settings --> Privacy to change the settings. 
VIP servers are private servers that some games allow being bought for Robux (Roblox's currency) but to get Robux, you either have to buy it with cash, or subscribe to Builders Club with cash. For Builders Club, you have to click the three dots on the left corner of the screen and click upgrade now at the bottom. Once there you can review the perks, and consider allowing it for your child. Robux can be bought by clicking the icon that looks like this: R$, there you can decide whether your child can purchase the Robux or not. If you allow it, then complete the transaction
Some YouTubers post "Free Robux Hack" or "Free Builders Club Hack" But hey are fake. If you catch your child watching these videos please make sure they do not follow the steps, as it could lead to them being hacked.
If you want to enable maximum security for your child's account, go to Settings --> Security where you can add e-mail verification and a PIN, make sure your child does not learn the PIN or else they could disable some privacy settings that could lead to their account being hacked.
E-mail verification asks for verification every time their child logs in from a new source, you can enable it to trust said device for 30 days, PINS ask for the PIN every time you change a setting, when you are done, a lock icon will appear at the top of the screen, click it once to enable security once again.
If your child is being bullied/harassed you can block them by typing in their username, going to their profile, clicking the three dots and clicking "Block User"

I will not review games because, if you have stuck around and read this, Account Restrictions will stop players for accessing inappropriate content

I hope you enjoyed my review!

column6:
WHAT IS ROBLOX?
Roblox is a creative and fun platform which can be used to play with your friends, explore interesting games or even learn Lau code.

RECOMMEND?
Roblox is a game I have been playing for almost 6 years now. I would 100% recommend this game to anyone around the age of 8+. I do also recommend that if your child is between the ages of 1 - 13, they should have parental controls on. It will automaticly be turned on if you are under 13 but if you fake your age to turn it off, it is your responsibility, not Roblox Corp.

SAFE?
Roblox Corp. has done lots of work to iron out swear words, scams and bots to the platform, it has become a much safer environment for kids to play on. As lots of parents/kids have said that the game is littered with swear words, bypasses and sex releated subjects, these are considered to be false. Although you could bypass the swear  system, it is almost unrecognizable. If you are worried that your child is not swear free enough, I recommend turning off chat for them, located in the settings button of their account. Roblox Corp. does remove sex related games created by other people as fast as they can as they do not mean to have these games up for children to see, Roblox do not create the games that you child plays. As for violence, make sure you check weekly on what you child  is playing if you are worried that they could be playing violent games.

GAMES :
Roblox is a platform where YOU can create the games that go on the website and if they get popular, you could earn real life money using the dev exchange (more on that on the MONEY : section). You start of with a baseplate and you can add things made by other people from the workshop (any inappropriate models will get removed instantly). The game incourges you to learn code such as Lau (Google it) it is an advanced but simple to master code. Unlike websites such as 'Scratch', the code used in Roblox Studio is very similar to Python.

MONEY :
In Roblox, there is a currency called 'Robux'. To put it simply, you can buy robux from the robux store and you or your child can use it to buy items from the catalog such as hats and shirts + more! Robux can also be used to buy gamepasses for games which give you special perks in the game. In roblox, you can also get a membership called RobloxPremium (previously known as builders club). With this you will receive robux monthly, different amounts depending on what package you buy. You would pay for RobloxPremium monthly. You can also get many other perks with it as well, more info on the RobloxPremium page.

Dev Exchange is a way to cash out robux and put it into real money. (100,000 robux = $350 | 600,000,000 robux = $2,000,000. To put it simply, you can become millionaires on roblox! Why wouldn't you? You must be over 13 to use this feature in roblox but it is a great feature to use. If you create a game or shirt, you can earn robux from it. A team of developers called 'Badimo' used their robux from a game they made called 'Jailbreak' and converted it in to real life money. They managed to pay of their college funds with it! Sounds great!

SUM UP :
Overall, roblox is a fun platform for all! Although it may have it's flaws, the game itself, is a game you or your child should not miss.

Usually, older players who have learned Lua create the games. Chances are, your kid might eventually ask for Robux. As I mentioned earlier, Robux is a digital currency on Roblox that can be purchased with real money. Being a kid, I have asked for Robux, but my parents never let me purchase them. However, there are other ways to get Robux for free. Websites that promise free robux are fake. However, players can create games and charge robux for access. When another player purchases access, the seller will receive "pending robux". After 1-3 business days, the robux will transfer to the players account. Selling access to a game for 25 robux translates to 3 pending robux, therefor giving the seller 3 robux. This is very little and can purchase only a few things on the platform. Selling gamepasses in your game, however, results in much more pending robux. Selling gamepasses for 500 robux will translate to 350 pending robux, which is a lot. Overall. a great game for kids. Roblox is a very fun game that I recommend for anybody in 1st grade and above. It is a very interesting game with lots of variety that can appeal to all people. HOWEVER, there are some common misconceptions about it:
-
-PLEASE OPEN THE FULL REVIEW TO READ, THANKS!-
-
DOES ROBLOX INCLUDE DATING?: Most of the time, NO! There will always be people who attempt to online date no matter where you go on the internet. Teach your child what is appropriate and what isn't.

DOES ROBLOX INCLUDE SWEARING?: For children aged 12 and under, ALMOST NEVER! It is extremely hard to bypass the chat filters built for children under the age of 13. There is an extremely low chance that your child will be exposed to any inappropriate words/phrases worse than "hell" or "idiot."

DOES ROBLOX INCLUDE INAPPROPRIATE BODY MOVEMENTS?: Pretty much NO. Unless you count typically fully-clothed characters doing kid-friendly dances next to each other, it is unlikely that your child will come across bad stuff like this.

DO I HAVE TO PAY FOR ROBLOX?: NO, unless your child wants to purchase a wide range of accessories/clothing for their avatar, but there are lots of free accessories/clothing already! They can also purchase special powers in different Roblox games. HOWEVER: In order to purchase Robux (Roblox currency), your child must read a warning explaining that they are about to spend real money.

DOES ROBLOX INCLUDE VIOLENCE?: A LITTLE BIT. The default and widely-used effect of dying in-game is your character falling apart onto the ground, with no blood and/or gore. Some games do include weaponry and/or fighting, but it does not get too violent.

MY CHILD EXPERIENCED SOMETHING INAPPROPRIATE ON ROBLOX!: I am sorry to hear that. However, Roblox games that are scripted to allow inappropriate things are usually taken off of Roblox within hours. Speak with your child and educate them on what is and isn't appropriate.

column6:
I have played Roblox for three years now, and I do like it a lot. Younger kids will love the game while older kids while love making their own games like me. In this review, I’ll be covering every CSM topic. Apologies for the bad format, CSM breaks it.

(Educational Value)
Roblox’s greatest educational value comes from Roblox Studio, it’s in-house game development engine every game on the platform is built with. Despite its minor flaws, I love using Roblox Studio, and I have made some successful games that other people have played. Roblox Studio is best suited for older kids, as younger kids will not understand the engine that will be fairly complex for them. 
As for the main platform, it is up to individual games for what educational value they want to have.

(Great messages)
See below.

(Great role models)
Not much to say here, role models vary from game to game. As a platform, Roblox seeks to encourage the learning of programming and 3-D modeling.

(Easy to play/use)
Despite a few outliers, he vast majority of user-created games are simple to play, which is why Roblox has such a large fanbase of children. Roblox Studio on the other hand can take months to learn, in my case, almost two years to fully feel comfortable.

Too much violence
The amount of violence in a game varies from game to game, but Roblox does limit the extent. Excessive gore is prohibited, and games that include it are taken down often. Games that Roblox see as glorifying violence and other related topics such as recreating tragic world events such as the Holocaust and 9/11 are prohibited.

Too much sex
Roblox encountered widespread media coverage around 2018 of the emergence of sexually explicit games on the platform, but the corporation has since taken extreme actions against them. The genre of games, known in the communities as “condos,” are an effectively extinct species. If a player is not looking for them, there is an extremely, extremely low chance they will ever find them. Even if they do search for it, they will not show up in results. Rumors have sent the perpetrators of these inappropriate games running, as rumors have it Roblox has began to threaten legal action against those continuously breaking Roblox’s rules on explicit content.

Too much swearing
Roblox has an extremely strict chat filter that replaces words or phrases seen as problematic with a random number of “######.” Some examples of what the filter looks for includes profanity, addresses, phone numbers, and occasionally certain names. Some players will attempt to bypass this filter by using foreign characters and intentional misspellings, but they can be reported to moderators where they face bans and terminations.

Too much consumerism
Roblox’s only official currency is Robux, which serves a widespread purpose. On the platform side, hats, clothing, accessories, etc. can be purchased with Robux, as can user-generated-content. On the game side, developers of games can create gamepasses which are essentially in-app purchases that work only in that certain game. Robux is quite pricy, as the cheapest purchasing option is eighty Robux for one US dollar, and the next being four-hundred Robux for five US dollars. I’d say the average gamepass in someone’s game will usually cost around four-hundred Robux, and the average hat will cost around fifteen to one-hundred Robux. Robux can also be made by selling gamepasses in one’s own game, although the Roblox company takes a percentage cut. Additionally, developers can make extra Robux through premium payouts when players with Roblox’s optional subscription service play their game. Robux earned through development can even be converted into real money if a lot is accrued, although the process is complicated, with requirements such as a tax form to fill out. An unfortunate side effect of being able to make money from Roblox game development is pay-to-win games that promote buying expensive gamepasses. A prime example of this is Pet Simulator X, the most popular game at the time of writing. Pet Simulator X will be releasing a real-life plushie that comes with an in-game bonus for the Pet Simulator X game on Roblox. How much does this giant, highly sought-after plushie cost? Two-hundred-and-fifty dollars. Actually, it was supposed to be one hundred bucks more expensive, and the developer only changed it after backlash. Pretty much, pay attention to the value of what you are buying. 

A WARNING TO PARENTS
By far Roblox’s biggest problem is exploitation of children by scammers and creeps. Please read this to be aware of the rare, but real danger. Number one, and the worst, grooming. There have been rare, but documented claims of attempted grooming by adults towards impressionable children. It is very important to note that Roblox is only the gateway. The actual grooming never happens on Roblox only begins. The predator will meet the victim on Roblox, maybe friend them, talk to them in the private chat, but no harm will be done with Roblox’s inability to send images and the strong chat filter. How the predator exploits the child is by leading them away from Roblox and onto a separate service, most often Discord. Discord is a fantastic app that is great for talking with people and forming a community, but it is supposed to be for those thirteen and older, and has no filter or safety protections. Please monitor your child’s activity on Roblox. There are some safety precautions you can take. If a Roblox user’s age is set to under thirteen, the chat filter is stronger. Additionally, private messages can be blocked, highly reducing the already extremely low chance of encountering a creep. There are many others I don’t have time to get into, but definitely check out the settings, they are your best friend. Another problem with Roblox is scams. Robux is a highly sought after resource for kids, and they will really do anything to get their hands on a new outfit. Sadly, the lowest scum on Earth will try to trick your kids. There are several methods you should be aware of. First, off-site. Well, there are two types. There are the flat-out scams, and the sketchy sites. The first is the dying breed. They promise free Robux when you click the button. Spoiler alert, it doesn’t work any you might have just gotten a computer virus, The second is the sketchy sites, which actually do give you Robux when you complete surveys. However, these survey websites are probably doing illegal activities and are collecting personal data on your child. Also, the Robux was probably not obtained legitimately. And of course, this is all highly against Roblox’s rules. The second method of scams is in-game, where scammers will use the advertise game feature to promote a fake game posing as the official Roblox account. They will have a fraudulent but real-looking game that asks your child to put in their username and password to get free Robux, but obviously all you get is an account stolen. Fortunately, Roblox has gotten much, much better at taking these games down before hardly anyone can get scammed.

(Conclusion)
Roblox is not a perfect platform, especially one with so many users. Roblox has a lot to deal with, but in recent months and years, there has been a very noticeable increase in safety. The future is bright with this platform.

Roblox is a great game. There's many good things about it, but there are downsides.

The pros:
 - You can interact with other people, play together (some people may consider it a con)
 - There's MANY different games on Roblox, which means a lot of choice. (Roblox itself shouldn't be called a 'Game'. I would prefer to think of it as a library filled with games.)
 - Different games on Roblox can bring different benefits. There's games like 'chess', 'stackables' (Jenga) and more. Of course, they are just virtual and are way different in the real world. 

Cons:
 - Some people may be bad. Of course, you never know who's on the other side. Tip (for other kids): Don't tell anyone info about yourself online. If someone asks for your age, you shouldn't try it.
     Types of bad people online:
         - People that swear. Although roblox has a chat filter, some 
            people can overcome it by changing the letters. Like 'Sh0t' or 
            even worse words. If you see a person like that, try reporting (I'll 
            talk about it in a while)
        - People that ask for personal info. The chat filter blocks numbers 
           too (and it may be annoying sometimes) but try your best not to 
           give it away. And now for parents, don't overreact. Not all people 
           online are bad. Most people aren't. Just teach your child how to 
           react/what to do when they encounter someone like them. And 
           banning them from playing won't really solve the problem (really). These types 
           of people are rare (in my opinion). I met only 1 person asking for my age (I 
           started playing 3 years ago but didn't really talk to anyone, and now know 
           more on how Roblox and it's community works) I, of course didn't give them 
           my age, reported them, and left the game.

           Here's an example of a conversation with a person of that type (it heavily 
           depends on the personality of your child, and it may differ. This is the 
           conversation I had with the person):
P - Sketchy Person
M or I - Me
RP - Random person.

P sits next to me. (In a game)
P: Hello!
M: Hi.
P: Nice avatar! (the player's look, you can customize it)
M: Thanks!
P: You must be rich!
M: Nah, not really, I don't overexaggerate.
P: Ok.
P sends me a friend request
I accept for some reason.
The person seemed nice.
After a while the person said 'Hey!'
M: Hi.
P: How old are you?
At this point I feel that something is off. 

M: Why do you need to know?
P: Why not?
M: Why yes?
P: Come on, just tell me.
M: Why?
P: Just tell me a number.
M: Can I have some privacy? I'd rather not tell you.
P: Please.
M: No.
RP joins the conversation.
RP: Why do you need to know? Leave this person (me) alone.
P leaves the game.
After a few minutes I find P's profile and report him/her.

Reporting and moderation:

The report system on Roblox rarely works. It's most likely because the moderators have a lot of work to do, if that's the case, Roblox should hire more of them.

The automatic report system may break sometimes, causing false warning and banning. An example of it is that I tried uploading a pitch black shirt to Roblox, it got removed, and I got warned. But why? For being 'inappropriate'? I don't get it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Consumerism.

Kids can spend a LOT of money on Robux, Roblox's virtual currency. Maybe your child begged you for robux. I kind of get the point. You can make your avatar way more decorated and look nice. You can buy gamepasses that let you get, for example, a scooter in-game. When you buy them the Robux, tell them to try their best to save it and not spend it all.

I know, this review is quite long, thanks for making it to the end.

I know Roblox can be an unsafe environment for younger children, but in my experience I've had relatively minor (but still alarming) issues. It honestly depends on which server you play in (which game you choose). For example, there have been no issues on 'Feather Family' (a bird roleplay game, where you play as a bird and interact with other players to make a story), but both of the incidents I've experienced have been on 'Brookhaven' (an open human roleplay server). Set in a small town with upper-class vibes, players can choose a job (from SWAT team to YouTuber), name their in-game customizable avatar, and acquire a house or apartment. The incidents in question are as follows: a player presenting as male offered to be my bodyguard (after several occurrences of children breaking into my house) and so I gave him roommate permissions (he could unlock the door to my house and possibly also change other house-related settings). He disappeared while I went on a wild goose chase to find one of the kids who broke into my house, and upon finding the offender, I tried to locate my 'bodyguard'. When I finally did, just up the road, he pulled out a gun and told me he was going to (unalive) me. This, of course, caught me off guard and I left the game without saying anything. It was hard to tell if he was joking, or if it was just part of the roleplay. It's a shock that, while messages like "I told you" get blocked, the words "I'm going to kill you" still get through. There are some major issues with this system. The second incident was on the same server. My roleplay character presented as male this time, and I posted on a billboard that I was looking for a roommate. Almost immediately, I got a response from a player presenting as female. She greeted me with a "hey 😏" and once she had given me roommate permissions to her house, she immediately asked whether or not I had a "girl" (resulting in me logging off immediately again). I think the big problem with these games is that a lot of kids and possibly teenagers are looking for "Roblox girlfriends" or "Roblox boyfriends", which can make them easy prey for predators. Make sure you monitor your child, and I'd recommend that they stay away from Brookhaven. ///////

Edit: As a side note, watch out for Robux purchases and processes (the in-game currency paid for by real money). My brother is nine and constantly wants to buy more Robux, as in a majority of the games he plays on Roblox have things to be purchased built in. Look out for that.

Edit 2: Look out for servers where players can "donate" Robux to each other. It seems as if most people on these servers are trying to scam people, or simply spam the chat with repetitive, cookie-cutter phrases to encourage others to donate to them. One player's "stand" was obviously hacked to me, but it might not have been as obvious to young children. When I clicked on an item that stated its cost as five Robux, I was confused as to why it showed the balance on my account went way down if I chose to purchase said item. ("Your balance after this purchase will be 56 Robux.") Then I realized that, even though it said I'd be paying five, the mediator screen showed I'd have to pay 299 Robux! There were several other things wrong with that player's stand, but I'll leave it at that. I reported them and pointed out their scam to them in chat. Additionally, their avatar looked like a fully-grown man with no idea of what teenage girls like to put on their Roblox figures put together what he thought was the most "attractive" outfit. //////

Edit 2 (cont'd): There are also many issues with the moderation system. Words like "ass" and "hell" come through, but the words "bro" and "ok" get censored. There have been several occasions where someone spams the chat with potty language or repetitive sentences. Please monitor your child while using this app/game if you would not like them to be exposed to such occurrences.

If you're an overprotective parent who came over to Common Sense Media to see if this video game that your child keeps talking about is actually safe, then this review is for you.

In my opinion, it's safe to say that Roblox is definitely safe for your kid(s).

First off, most of the top reviews in the parent's review section were from 2-3 years ago, when Roblox's chat filter wasn't the best. The chat filter now is a lot better than it was 2-3 years ago. I can confirm since I've been playing Roblox for a few years now. Obviously, no chat filter in the world is 100% clean. I would say that the Roblox chat filter filters out the bad words 99.2% of the time. I say 99.2% because in a VERY rare situation, some person will use a special character to fill in for a bad word. This has only happened to me ONCE in the last 5 years that I have been playing Roblox.

Plus, in your account settings, you can choose whether or not you want to see chat in games.

Second, I just want to clarify that Roblox is not a game, it's a platform. The difference is that Roblox staff doesn't make the games (excluding Roblox game events & games that Roblox made back in 2006). The reason I say that is because parents were complaining that some games that their child was playing was disgusting, and they couldn't believe that Roblox moderators would allow this type of content. You won't find too many of these games anymore, unless you REALLY try to find them. Plus, I've never in my life have ever found or played a Roblox game that had "suggestive" themes in it. 

Thirdly, Roblox moderation. Roblox moderation has improved so much over the last couple of years that I think many people take granted for. Sure, Roblox moderation could be better at taking down games faster and banning people who say naughty things. But remember, Roblox is on the brink of reaching 2 billion users, not to mention the billions of games Roblox moderators have to look over. So it's very hard for Roblox moderators to look at every single report they get.

Lastly, I have learned many real world stuff just from Roblox. I am a rather small developer on the platform and really enjoy connecting with my friends online. I have made quite a lot of robux off of my games, and I'm planning on one day making real life money from Roblox legally. (It's called DevEx. Search it up if you don't know what I'm talking about.)

Conclusion : Roblox is a very epic game. I recommend you tell your kid to not tell strangers about your address or other personal information. 
Other than that, I give Roblox 5 stars.

After joining this game back in 2010 a lot has changed over the years. When I joined, the developers and admin team actually enforced rules, people were creative with their game ideas, and the community wasn't as toxic as it is today. Now in 2018, this game has become unplayable and not enjoyable. I understand that over the years Roblox had become bigger and had to be more kid friendly which is fine. But instead of trying to make games and express creativity, this game has become a social media site with excessive amounts of toxicity. Over the years, Roblox has tried to fix their issues with implementing updates that did nothing but drive away the veteran players such as myself. For example, they implemented a chat filtering system to cut back on the amount of swearing which is good, but the filtering system got so bad that I can't even say numbers or specific words that have nothing to do with a bad context. But even before the filter, the admin team would kick and enforce rules to those who even said an abbreviation or derivative of a swear word. 

Over my experience, I have composed a list of what not to do in this game due to safety issues.

1. Do not spend money or buy builder's club memberships. If you buy these with a credit card, you will become a big target for hackers who will steal your information. 

2. Do not give out any personal information such as age, location, or anything along those lines. Its okay to have friends, but make sure they are only your friends on Roblox and not in real life unless you personally know them. 

3. Make sure you do not give out passwords to people since they will go to your account and take it over, spend your money on your credit cards, and whatever else they feel like doing. 

Bullying Concerns: Even though there is bullying going on in the real world and online, there is a button called "block a player" or something along those lines which will block a player from communicating to you, and I believe there is an in-game mute button to mute players.  Those above a few ways to limit or prevent bullying. 

Consumerism: This game before was a favorite for many since there was an opportunity to play the game and buy all the cool stuff for free. Each day you logged in, you would get tickets which could be converted into Robux or used to buy things such as in-game clothing, hats, gear, and other interesting things. This game has always been free, but if you want to look cool or look anything like they do in the commercials, you need to spend money. The prices for these extra things are not cheap either and will burn holes through your pockets. For example, there is a pirate hat that is about 2,000 Robux, which in USD is around $25. Builder's Club Membership is nice, but will make you a big target for hackers. There are 3 levels of Builder's Club and each will give you more benefits than the other, but for more money. This link is for each level and it's benefits. https://www.roblox.com/premium/membership?ctx=leftnav
A cool feature to this game is the limited items market and trading. It works like the economy where you need money to start up your business and a risk/benefit factor. Then you can trade and sell items to make profits, but you need builders club and you will need Robux to start which is a double whammy. If you are successful, you will probably never have to spend money on this game since some of the items are worth $1,000s in real life.

Game-Creating: This game is also nice because you can make your own games, but if they get popular you can make money with a Developer Exchange Program where you can make good money, but it will take a lot of hard work. Once again, you would need Builder's Club to participate in that program. https://www.roblox.com/develop/developer-exchange
This link will show you requirements and other things having to do with the Developer Exchange. They are really stupid in my opinion. 

Online-Dating Issues: Online Dating on Roblox has always been an issue around the 2011-2012 time period and is still going strong to this day. Roblox may become a hotspot for sexual predators if it hasn't already since this game is becoming huge and popular. The problem is that kids and teens will try to go out with someone they don't know. They will never know who that person is until they meet them on the street, and after you meet them, you are screwed. Word of advice, don't do it, and if someone tries to pressure you, then you need to block them and/or leave the game and go to a different server. 

Overall Summary: This game isn't the game it used to be and gets a ton of hate due to its current state unfortunately. This game back in 2011ish and before was great since it was a smaller community and it didn't have so much toxicity even though its always been around. Consumerism has taken a toll on the community and it seems that little to none care about the community anymore. The updates Roblox comes out with are usually for the worst instead of the best. Online-Dating is still a huge issue that many seem to either care or not care about. 

Thank you for reading this!

You might think that flying games are boring. However, if you’re going to say that flying games are boring, you’re either lying or you’ve never played PTFS. Unlike most other flight games, PTFS is detailed and shows high effort from the developer. It has realistic and minimalist detail and has incredibly high-quality lighting. The plane models look realistic and spot-on with the real thing.
PTFS is also incredibly accessible - it’s free and is easy to play, with an informative tutorial. 
This game is definitely worth your time. It has leading variety and high fun level, has an unrivaled attention to detail and graphics, and appeals to more than just one target audience. It stands out among the disease that is: the huge lack of originality.

column6:
I have been playing Roblox for a long time now and I LOVE IT. I read through the reviews people are putting on here about people "cursing, sex, and violence", and I truly don't understand. When you sign up your child for Roblox it will ask you how old they are and if you want "SafeChat" on. I HIGHLY recommend this for parents if you have children ages 10 and under, because this does a lot in blocking out inappropriate content. My parents did this and until I was 13 (I am now 14, and still adore Roblox) and until we turned it off, I could not do or see the following things on my account:

- Enter numbers on chat; if someone is trying to get your child's information they will be unable to put it in the chat if their chat is on (you could just turn off the chat until you think they are at an age where they can protect themselves online though)
- See explicit content on the app; your child will be unable to join any game on Roblox that has heavy violence, sex or drug references.
- Type or see inappropriate words in chat; your child will not be able to say any explicit words or look at them in the chat if another player tries to say a bad word (while there are ways to get around Roblox on chat for older kids WITHOUT SafeChat, such as spaceing your word out or using numbers, my sister has a younger child account, and we have tested if she can see these kind of things, and she can't. A bunch of #### will appear, even if they try to get around it by spaceing). 

Here's what I have to say about the so-called "hacking" going on. The website https://roblox.com, HAS NEVER BEEN HACKED. What actually CAN be hacked is your Roblox ACCOUNT. If you have a super simple password like `12345dog, I can pretty much say with certainty, YOU WILL GET HACKED. Think of a strong password you will remember, BUT is NOT something like your name, age, pet, favorite animal, or address/former addresses. Hackers can easily find these kind of things on the internet. I have been on this game for 3 years and I have NOT ONCE been hacked EVER, because I have a strong password. 

The people saying that "my child spends to much time on it" or "my kids addicted to it", YOU ARE THE PARENT! Your the one responsible for setting the limit on how much time your child is spending on devices. You can fix this on your own. Try setting a screen time limit on the device. 

If you have a Apple device:
- You can set a limit on any app you want for a certain amount of time every day from your child's iCloud (which I'm assuming you have one, since it's required to set up an iPad). My parent's did this for me for years. I never spent more than an hour and a half on Roblox, or four hours on my iPad overall. And if you want to let them have a few more minutes, they can send a request for more time that you choose how much to give out of 15 minutes, 1 hour, or all day. You can set more restrictions as well, such as websites, app downloads, and even who they contact.

On a Android (Google, Samsung, Etc.) device:
- If you have an Android, you can do the same as above. There are a few differences, like how for giving more screen time YOU pick the amount of time and once the time is out, it's for everything except emergency's, but overall they pretty similar to each other. To set it up, you'll have to reset your child's device, create a child google account with the restrictions you prefer, link this account to your Google account, and sign their new account onto the device while setting it up. Really great way to protect your child's internet usage, My parent's and I both ABSOLUTELY LOVED it!

 I HIGHLY recommend Android's version of screen time for many reasons though as compared to Apple's. For one thing, during the years I had an Android, It was much easier for my parents to make sure that I was safe online. The website, screen time, and app download restrictions they set were very stable, unlike Apple's, which sometimes I was able to access things restricted or have as much time as I pleased. Also, if your child accidentally/purposefully visits a site that is restricted or inappropriate, it alerts you in your email. This happened to me when I was about 9 years old, my parent's were alerted by Google, came to me and discussed what I saw so I could understand (it was like a porn website or something like that), and were able to resolve the issue. I didn't know what to do, and I was too scared to say what I had seen. If my parent's weren't alerted to the matter, I could've been scarred for life.

All in all, if your nervous about your child being on Roblox, I hope this helps so your child can have as much fun and imagination as I did!

Scam games and websites DO exist, do not get fooled by so called "Free Robux and/or Premium", and use common sense, because somethings might look too good to be true, Roblox staff would NEVER ask you for your credentials, if you find something too good to be true, it most likely is, plus people make these scam games, for example: If you see a game on Roblox saying if you buy a game pass from that game you will get rare pets in Adopt Me, tell your kid it's too good to be true and inform DreamCraft about it,  and remember to be mindful that some games sell one life items for robux (AKA Items that you will lose upon respawning) and temporary perks (Perks you can buy but will expire after some time, such as paid VIP servers or EXP boosters), I cannot stress this enough, but you need to always know the content of games that your children is about or is already playing to determine if that game is good for them or not, and please tell your children to not play (Insert game title here) because of (Insert reason here), and finally... Roblox moderation is not perfect, nor is the community, because I have seen cases when someone should get hit with the ban hammer and they didn't, including people who should not and did. so don't be mad if your child got their account suspended or completely terminated since you can always appeal, I recommend you wait out suspensions and only appeal to account terminations (Remember to speak to your kids that it is wrong to do something like that if they have been suspended or terminated for a good reason, plus you can also request to Roblox to terminate your kid's account, but that should be reserved as a last resort)

column5: Great, especially games you find from your own interests
column6:
This is a great game, especially if you find the right kind of games. I’ve been playing since 3rd grade so I have a few tips for kids and parents.
Most of the front page games aren’t worth playing, but there are tons of games that you can find that are really good. If you are on the younger or more relaxed side, Bee Swarm Simulator, Build a Boat for Treasure, Cabin Crew, and Natural Disaster Survival are great. Since there is less competition in those types of games, there will be less toxicity and rude players. If you are the competitive type, Phantom Forces, Elemental Battlegrounds, and Blackhawk Rescue Mission 5 are also good games. BRM5 is a personal favorite due to the fact that the enemies aren’t other players (they’re NPCs), so there’s more of a focus on teamwork. I could go on and on but the best way to find good games is by searching keywords you like (e.g. “flight simulator”) and check out the games that you find, or by looking at videos and reviews about games and see what you find.
Violence-wise, each game differs. The closest thing to gore they often allow is either a 2D texture of blood or an almost flat red cylinder. A lot of the negative reviews about the violence on here is “I saw my 12 year old shoot a zombie with a gun! I banned it from my child for life!” It’s basically the same as a Nerf gun or water balloons in real life. Nobody actually gets hurt but you still have fun.
If you see someone who is rude, just ignore them. Having a thick skin is imperative, but if they cross a line you can report them. Some parents complain about people bypassing the chat filter with @ or $. There’s more cussing on a school bus. If you or your child ever goes out to public places like school or the grocery store, you will hear cussing. It’s not nice but it’ll happen no matter how sheltered a child is.
Finally, about the transactions, it is heavily recommended that you go to Walmart or Dollar General and get a gift card for that instead of using a credit card. I walk there occasionally and use my own money that I earned, instead of begging my parents.
It is overall great and I think 3-4th grade is a good time to start.

For parents

I bet you've heard some great and nasty things about this game, and they're all true. Roblox is great if you have proper guidance. If you let your kid know what to do and what not to do, you won't have problems. Bad stuff happens when you leave a kid unchecked online. Roblox does do a pretty bad job with their moderation, though. Here are a few things that if you do use them, you'll have no problems.

1. Check regularly on what your kid is doing. Your kid might not like this, but you need to check their "Continue Playing" category and their messages. If you see anything that doesn't seem right, ask them about it or search it up.
2. Make sure you have proper restrictions and settings. When making a  child's account, if they are under 13, make their age under 13. This info is private and somewhat prevents mature content. Also make sure the device your on has proper parental controls, especially if it's a phone/tablet. If you don't do this, the next person whose kid spent $6000 dollars could be you, and I'm sure you don't want that to happen.
3. Games to stay away from. Most games on Roblox are great, and fun to play, but a few aren't so bright and friendly. Here's a short list of games you most definitely should avoid. 
- Da Hood. Just from the name, you should know this is a gang-based game with much violence and gore.
- Any "Boys and Girls Hangout type game". These games are a cover for online daters and pedophiles. Just stay away.
- Ragdoll Simulator. RS is an actually great game, but recently it has developed a problem with mass amounts of toxic players there. These people are very toxic, and generally terrible people.
4. Teach your kid about online safety. There are many people on Roblox who will try to get information about you, or scam you. The most popular game, "Adopt Me", has a massive scammer problem. Tell your kid that if they are ever going to "Trade" someone, to call you over to have a look. Get them to tell you the value of the items, and if they don't know, search it up. Ok, before you click of of this review because I am just a teen with no sense of what it is like to be a parent, hear me out. I will be giving a review with CURRENT and ACCURATE information, and some things that parents may think after reading the parents guide and have had their child play ROBLOX, that are most likely wrong. (Also please excuse my bad spelling and grammar in the review)

(1) The CommonSense Media Parental Guide: The CommonSense Media Parental Guide is EXTREMELY outdated, and I want you to put this in your mind before reading it. First of all, they mention some things about "forums". When forums existed, they were like forums on any other social media, and why I say "when they existed," is because ROBLOX RETIRED FORUMS IN 2017! They no longer exist, and you do not need to worry about them and their dangers. Also, the guide says a lot of incorrect things, but the one that spiked my attention the most is when it said how poorly ROBLOX moderated ODers, now if you don't know what an ODer is, ODer = Online Dater. But, ROBLOX now does a much better job in moderating them (I mention this in my section about them later in the review.) And along with preadators and condo games, ROBLOX also does a very, very good job in moderating them (more about that in the ODer section of my review.) And! Builders Club also does not exist! It was replaces recently by "premium" although do not worry, since your child will probably not want to get it, since the only benefits are that you can join more ROBLOX groups, make clothing to sell, trade Limited Items (especially expensive items that make up an entire ROBLOX economy through the trading and selling of them.)

(2) ROBLOX Studio: ROBLOX Studio is a platform, well to be more specific the platform your child can use to design games, improving coding skills and teaching them other things. Although I will say ROBLOX Studio is not as acessible as people make it seem, you've probably heard of this and you're probably looking for it in the Apple Store on your iPhone now. Well, you need a
Mac, Windows, or PC Computer to use it. It is NOT availible on any mobile or XBox devices. But, you probably have a computer your child can use, so if you or they are intested in learning coding your child should get this app and learn to code! They're are lots of helpful tutorials on YouTube, or if you don't trust some stranger on YouTube to teach your kid, they're are lots of classes with professionals that use ROBLOX to teach the Lua programming language (The code language ROBLOX uses.) So try it today! Teach your kids something useful!

(3) ROBLOX Games For Your Child: Now, here I will be talking about some ROBLOX games and the appropriate ages to use them for your child, because yes some games have a variety of directed audiences, some are meant for young children, some are meant for teens. (More on my section on the types and ages of ROBLOX users). 

(4) Game Reviews My First game I'll review is the most popular game on ROBLOX: Adopt Me, Adopt Me I'd say is for any child over the age of 8+ in the game, you get a pet and are required to do tasks for your pet to earn money to do things like buy houses and cars, and buy better pets! Which you can use to...scam people? Ok, YES Adopt Me is full of scammers and that's why I rated it so highly but as long as your child is properly educated on scams (teaching moment for parents) they will be fine! Now for my next game: Aresenal I rate Aresenal as 9+ Aresenal is a first person shooter game, now you're probably thinking "A shooting game!? Why isn't this rated for a more mature audience!?" And that is because of two words: Kill Effects, yes the game uses guns and before you start thinking of all those stories you hear of Serial Killers who played FPS games as a kid and turned phycho, yeah, that's a bunch of bullcrap. This game is not bloody or violent is anyway, except for the guns and knives you use to take out your enemies. And it is not bloody, there are different cartoony "kill effects" like one where you're enemy will fall down a trapdoor when you kill them or get hit by lightning. And, you may now be thinking, "Wait this just makes killing seem fun! You're freaking dumb!" Well I am not! If you think about it the game is an opportinuty to teach kids about violence in real life and how serious it is and how you shouldn't do it. My next game: Jailbreak, this game is where you can play as a criminal or a cop and I rate it 7+ and if you are a criminal your job is to escape prison, and rob assorted robbery places around the map like the bank or the power plant, and use the money you get from those things to buy guns and cars to help escape the police, and if you are a police you earn money by arresting criminals to buy guns and cars to help catch them. Now again, this is a teaching moment, you can teach your kids the seriousness of doing things like robbing places and escaping prison, and how cops are good people who are (supposed to anyway) protect us. Now after my reviews you can probably see the age that ROBLOX users are mostly.

column6:
So, I've seen slot of adults complain about Roblox so I'm gonna respond to ever major common point with a solution

1: "It promotes bullying."
Ok first of your child has probably dealt with a bully in real life before, so just because your child is behind a screen doesn't mean they're safe from bullying, heck it's even more frequent on the internet because people have a shield behind them, but it's also a whole lot easier to avoid them. Look you should educate a child about cyberbullying first before even letting them do anything on the internet, and second Roblox has multiple features to deal with bullying such as: 1. Blocking: Roblox has a built in block feature all you have to do is click the bullys username on the top right and click block user, this will stop the account from seeing anymore messages from the user.
2. Leave the server. If you're child is in a toxic environment leave the environment just click the 3 lines on the top left of the screen and then click leave server.
3. Report the user. Ok admittedly the report feature isn't the best but if your child wants to report a user to admins for severe bullying, send a report. Just click the three lines on the top left scroll down find he username and click the flag button than a menu will pop up select bullying and then right your message and it will get sent to a moderator. 

2. "There is too much swearing and it isn't censored enough."
The filter on Roblox is actually pretty strong and will block lots of profanity and more mature words, if a message is sent in hashtags (Example: ####) that means it has been filtered and blocked and yes sometimes you can guesa what they were trying to say on the context of their sentence but it's better than most filters and most Roblox players think it's TOO strict as it censors numbers and certain words in specific context but the filter is learning and will get better over time, but a few people do find loopholes not to get censored by the game, it's just like real life, every class had that one trouble maker that wouldn't follow the rules and try his best to break them, Roblox is no different and you if it bothers you just report him for swearing or leave the server.

3: "The clothing is too revealing"
Is this really that big of a deal, most of roblox's clothing is made by the community so I find it a bit unfair to blame it entirely on Roblox, most of this clothing cost robux anyway so u will have to spend real life money anyways to even get them, the most revealing free item is a minor crop top and if you're uncomfortable with your child wearing this clothing in Roblox tell them not to.

4: "To much sex and NSFW"
This is a flaw with user generated content, they will always be that one creep who makes those weird kind of things, however these
 games NEVER make it to the front page and Roblox is very strict on that kind of stuff and quick to ban these games so it's virtually impossible to find them unless your are specifically searching for one.

5: "Too much consumerism"
But it doesn't even force you to buy Robux (Roblox's digital currency) and the moderators of Roblox need to get paid somehow, same with game developers on Roblox. If your child somehow managed to spend some of your money than maybe your credit/debit card was added to the device most probably by you in the past and you forgot to remove it or to set it to require a password.

6: "It's easy to give out personal information"
Ok first off before your child even goes on the internet tell them not to give out any personal information and teach them what internet safety is. 2nd it's very hard to give out personal information on Roblox, Roblox censors phone number, emails and addresses along with most websites so probably the most personal information you'll be able to write is a name, and quick tip when your child makes a Roblox account tell them not to use their real names, Roblox even tells you not to. The only way your child will be able to give out any personal information is through other websites or services or bypassing the Roblox filter.

7: "My child is too addicted/My child's grades are lowering.
Ok first of incase you didn't know games feature puzzle solving, quick thinking and other things so they can actually be educational and 2nd off maybe you should tell your child to go out more often or make it where that can only play Roblox on weekends.

8. "Too much violence."
Yes some Roblox games contain violence but if you don't want them to play those games tell them not to and maybe give them a punishment if they do. You can check what game your child has played recently in the recently played section.

Ok now I'm gonna teach you how to make a Roblox account safe for your child.

1: Register an account with them make sure they don't use their real name in their username and make sure their date of birth is set correctly and you the parent should make the password to the account if you want your child to ask you every time they want to play.
2: Once your in click the gear on the top left and add your email immediately so your child's account can be safe and you'll be able to change their password if they do something wrong. In settings you can also disable chatting in game if you don't trust your child to not say anything personal or they're really young, this will also prevent your child seeing other people's messages in game.
3: Customize your child's avatar to something you and her are both comfortable with.
4: Play your first game, if you want to find a game for your child that you think is suitable then watch them play the game to determine its safe. Alternatively you can play these games I recommend:
Natural Disaster Survival: A game where you need to survive natural disasters.
Epic Minigames: A game full of lots of smaller fun games packed inside the most violent thing in the game is a sword fighting minigame but there is no blood.
Bee Swarm Simulator: A game where you have a swarm of bees and make honey, the most violent thing is that the bees will attack hostile animals that try to hurt you.
School Games (Royal High, Roblox High School and Robloxian High School): (Best played with chat permissions) A game where you socialize with people in a environment and play school related minigames, there is no violence but bullying could happen.

And that's my review I hope I atleast helped 1 parent out there when determining whether they should let their child play or not.

Thanks for reading this marathon of a review I guess.

Robux is roblox's virtual online currency which can be bought.

Sometimes people will bully you if you don't have robux, but not every server has that kind of behavior.

Robux scams are made possible with botted accounts that post comments on "group walls" that are something like "Want robux? Go to *scam website* and claim your reward now!" or "you have been the chosen one! claim soo much free adopt me awards and robux now! just go to *scam website* and claim now!!", there are also comments on item comment sections such as "this is a weird glitch post this on 3 different items then check your robux" which are ABSOLUTELY FAKE.

Another thing you should be aware of is "Condo games".
Now, if your child is under the age of 13, they won't be able to find these kind of games, because they're not approved by the roblox moderators and admins.
But you should still be careful, because if you dig deep into the game you might see a glance of sexual content.

There's also the broken report system, which works, but it's not great.
And the broken chat filters, which tag things (replace things with hashtags "#") such as "me too" by mistake. But the chat filters don't allow users under 13 to write numbers, I believe this is helpful, so they don't give out their phone number or similar, but it can also prevent alot of conversations, "there are # stages left until level #", "i hit ### followers yesterday!", etc.

EDIT: The Chat filter has been fixed! Users under 13 can say numbers! It's still a bit broken, but a big problem had been fixed!

The parents have alot of control over the child's account,
though one thing that's a flaw is you don't have to immediately enter your parent's email when you sign up, but it is optional to enter it once the account is created in the settings page.
But, the parents still do have good control.
You can turn on restrictions, which turn off the "contact settings", disallowing your child to chat with their friends while out of the game and participating in chat groups (different from normal groups).
I'm not sure about this, but I think you can also disable in-game chat for your child.
Overall, there's alot of options to secure your child's account, but it's not completely perfect.

There's also another problem, viruses in free models in roblox studio (roblox's tool to create games for other users to play), so you should probably monitor what models your child chooses to get.

Summary: It's good, but like any other app, you should be careful.
Thank you for reading!

Meep City is a game full of fun, it was one of the first games I played in Roblox. The game features customisable houses, fun activities and trading. Each player can communicate through the chat box , though be careful of what you read some might be too overwhelming or explicit. On the contrary, Meep City is a fun, colourful and easy game. I would highly recommend this game to anyone new to Roblox. For age groups I would allow kids older than 6 to play it, since it can get hard from time to time.

Jailbreak:

In the world of robbing or law, Jailbreak is the game that stands out from any other game. While playing the game you can start a robbery, or enforce the law and restore order into the city of Jailbreak. If you feel bored while playing, the game offers contracts for you to complete and with level you pass you get a prize. This game is more on the pricey side, but I can assure everyone that it is playable even when not spending a single Robuck. It has cool 3D buildings, amazing drivable vehicles and guns (if you’re into that). If you are someone who likes action and fun then Jailbreak is the perfect game for you to play. I would recommend this to kids over 8 or 9 years old.

Murder Mystery 2:

Sherif or Murderer? Who knows, but inside a world full mysteries no one can be certain of anything. Is the person you trust the most, the person that might to your downfall or vice versa. In MM2 you can buy skins by using in-game currency - by not using robuck/robux. Me and my friends play this three times a week and we never get bored, though this is on the more violent side it doesn’t show any blood that might traumatised younger players. So if you’re up for a mystery then MM2 is the game for you. Age-wise then I would recommend this to children 8 or 9 years old.

Retail Tycoon 2:

Are you interested in the retailing industry? Then Retail Tycoon 2 is the best game anyone could wish for. It has amazing cartoonish graphics and drivable vehicles. The game allows players to start their own shop, where they can sell food, furniture, technology and/or miscellaneous. Inside the game you will find multiple shops growing and bustling at their own pace, but its not the competition that decides your fate it’s you. So if you like being busy and very analytical then Retail Tycoon 2 is the perfect game.

In all the games I have listed in this review they are one of the most kid-friendly games, they are full of adventure and never run our of things to do (Jailbreak specifically). I have played Roblox since 2018 and my experience has been like no other. I wish more games likes these are added to Roblox, making competition for each developer/group to make strives towards making their game better. 

There are also some bad things about Roblox, like security breaches. So what my family has done to protect our account is to take advantage of all of Roblox’s security features, like 6 factor codes, email activation and using password automatically generated by Apple’s system. This ensures that my account and my family’s are protected against malware and/or hackers. If your kid is a big spender, I recommend using Apple’s family group feature where the parents or guardians can add credit card spending limits so they don’t over spend. The chat on Roblox can sometimes be very toxic so I heavily recommend playing with real life friends you know or have a good relationship with. With all this in mind Roblox can be the perfect child friendly game.

Here’s a nice little explanation of everything Roblox. After reading this, consider yourself as well-informed as the average Roblox nerd.. except only in that which matters to parents. ### First, what’s a Roblox? Roblox is not a video game. Roblox is more like a glorified app store, filled with portals to user generated ”experiences.” What makes Roblox different from the app stores? It has its own game engine, its own tools, its own moderation, and its own out-of-experience features. ### Roblox allows users to play these experiences together with random people and people they’ve added to their friend list. Chat functionality is a big part of Roblox, and it is moderated through the automatic moderation “tagging/hashing” (replacing with #s) bad parts of messages, or the whole message. ###Roblox’s moderation has changed a bit recently; users over and under 13 get different treatment. The user is trusted to give their real age, except for Voice Chat, which necessitates age verification. Voice Chat is available in supporting experiences (mostly hang out places; note: not all Roblox experiences are games) for users who have proven to be over the age of 13.
Players can private chat others they have added to their friends lists. This chat is moderated too, and players can also make group chats. ### Chat moderation can be bypassed if clever enough, but it is not easy to do so, and the bypassing player will almost always get in trouble with manual moderation afterwards. Do note that the player might get in trouble for harmless things and not for malicious things sometimes. ### Roblox has many extremely popular horror and violent experiences, such as Rainbow Friends, Doors, Arsenal, and Murder Mystery 3. ### Predators and otherwise dangerous people and content will always be present on any social platform of sufficient size. It is inevitable. I say inform your child, who is preferably around or over the age of 13, about what to avoid and how to stay safe; inform them not to tell others personal information such as age and location, and note that everybody on Roblox shares copious amounts of their own information, which results in social pressure to do the same. Do NOT give in, and remember that friends that you just play games with are very fun, and there is no need to speak of anything outside of the game to have a blast on Roblox, tell your child. And keep in mind: Dangerous things are found in dangerous places. Tell your child to be on high guard in hangout places and other social experiences, and make sure they don’t actively search for rule-breaking content. ### Like most online playground games, there are items available for purchase with virtual currency visible on Players’ avatars. Unlike other online playground games, unless the player becomes a creator and sells content (which requires skills no non nerd children possess), you cannot earn this currency (Robux) without spending some money. Experiences can also charge Robux for in-game perks. These purchases can be EXTREMELY tempting. ### Thanks for reading, and happy Robloxing!

column6: Roblox is often looked upon as inappropriate and poorly monitored. That is not the case at all, though. Roblox has many security features, such as a highly strict chat filter, inability to share social media links if the player is under 13, and a pin that parents can attach to the account which must be entered to change settings. You can also disable the chat within the settings, making it impossible for strangers to communicate with your children. Of course, like any game, there will always be immature players who find ways around the filter. For example, Roblox's chat filter prohibits numbers, but there are certain phrases that you can put before the number to make it visible (rbxp, grade, music, car, etc...), and some replace letters in swear words with symbols, such as turning "o" to "()", or "s" into "$". Again, this can be avoided by simply disabling the chat. As to violence, there are multiple games that involve attacking other players or NPCs. The weapons are often swords, guns, or knives, which aren't terribly realistic. However, I don't think that any type of violence, especially guns, is appropriate for younger kids, and that is why I think that Roblox should be 12+. In terms of sexual content, some online daters manage to use seemingly innocent animations and turn them into inappropriate positions. Roblox does take action against those who choose to abuse the animations. You can send a report to the moderators under anyone's username, however Roblox does not always read reports as much as they should. All in all, if you want your children to have a safe experience playing Roblox, simply monitor them and change their accounts' setting. If that's not enough, for whatever reason,  just don't let your kids play it. It's as easy as that.

column6:
One of the main ideas of Roblox is that you can make anything you want! However, some of the players want to make stuff that isn't so clean.

Is Roblox safe for your child? If he/she played every game, NO. Definitely not. If his/her game playing was monitored, yes, Roblox is great!
 
I'd like to say what's wrong with it. First off, games can get very gory and violent. One game that has been popular for many, many months is "Murder Mystery 2," which has a knife of the cover. It shouldn't be hard to guess this is inappropriate.

Almost every game has a chat box where players can communicate. Roblox works very hard to prevent all kinds of words and phrases, so that the game is safe. Whether it's a swear word or "I love you," Roblox will automatically cover it with hashtags. Even if you say something like
"w"
*new post*
"o"
*new post*
"r"
*new post*
"d"
Roblox can censor it! However, the company has not caught onto ALL of the kid's tricks. You can still find a couple loopholes here and there. The most common places for loopholes are modern role play games, like high schools, cities and cruise ships.

If you want to block out chat altogether, you can click to shrink the chat box, or even play in a "guest" account where no text is shown whatsoever.

On terms of money and addiction, there's quite a bit. I know I could easily spend HOURS on Roblox, probably even a whole day. Also, the game will entice players to buy an in-game currency called "Robux," costing about $1 per 100 Robux, as well as a membership.

Finally, I'd like to say that the idea is that you can make your own games, but you can't. The game maker is WAAAAYYY too complicated. However, your child MIGHT get motivated to make a game, and if they try hard and learn to coding language of Luna, congrats! They actually DID learn something!

Of course, most Roblox games still have minor violence, but it's more like taking apart a Lego minifigure than anything.

On terms of safety and fun, I recommend
Epic Minigames
Natural Disaster Survival
Freeze Tag
Work At A Pizza Place
Roblox Run
Flood Escape
Roblox Dodgeball
Speed Run 4
and Hide And Seek Extreme
I'd also like to mention MeepCity. It's a roleplay game, and people try to loophole a lot, but the creator works SUPER HARD on keeping things clean and appropriate, and has done an amazing job. There are still a few remaining kinks and loopholes, but I think after a year more of polishing, it should be close to all-the-way appropriate.

So for the bottom line: Moniter what your child plays, and Roblox should stay appropriate!

Scammers usually say to other players "get your free Robux" and some unwary players get scammed by these people. The scammers usually ask people for their passwords to add "free Robux," and then, when the password is given, they just steal all of the unwary player's Robux. Hackers are even worse. Without you even knowing, hackers not only steal your Robux, but also steal in-game money. This actually happened to my friend once. Although scammers and hackers are rare, you could still get hacked. Also, in some games, there is a little bit of violence, such as guns or killing, but this is very cartoonish, so I think even a 8 year old can handle this. Otherwise, I think Roblox is a good, entertaining game if you understand a little about these scammers and hackers and know the basic procedures.

Hope to see you on Roblox!

column5: ROBLOX; Great for learning and for making friends, but take caution!
column6:
Hi, I'm kidskool, a 10 year ROBLOX Veteran, reading the reviews. I believe what I have to say may be lost in the crowd, but I do hope it transmits the message I'm hoping to send: Let's start with the cons; 

1, Pricing: Let's get serious here, having players pay for a virtual currency is really off-putting to some Parents, from one of the reviews I read, the Parent was Double Charged for a perk ("Builders Club") and was very irritated on that matter, I may provide an answer to the problem: If you bought a single month Builders Club membership and you used a Credit or Debit Card to pay, it automatically renews every month. To prevent this, just simply send an email to ROBLOX ("info@roblox.com") just introduce yourself, who your Child's account is, what perk you purchased and that you wish to cancel the automatic renewal. 

2, Other Players: Okay, I've gone through it too. There are players on there ("Trolls") who's main reason for being online is to ruin the fun and enjoyment of other players. Reviews have claimed that the Staff of ROBLOX ("Moderators") don't pay attention to these reports, and when they look at them. They don't do anything, I understand the irritation. I've dealt with the Moderation on several cases, and I've had my cases solved, but I understand why it may be difficult for ROBLOX to handle all the requests. They only have so many Moderators to take care of all the members. Some moderators are tasked with screening user-uploaded decals, shirts, pants and T-Shirts, some are tasked with reviewing the site's forum. So I understand both parties problems. Another problem with players is the online role-playing and dating. With the role-playing it's just like in real life, they become whomever they wish. Which does provide some Anonymity, only problem with that is, some games also allow dating. I've seen these kind of games, and how players go around dating; "say 123 for hot gf" or "say 321 for bf", etc, etc.. While it is against the rules of ROBLOX, these are Children most cases. They try and cheat the system, using words that the computer doesn't recognize as dating phrases, this also goes along with swearing. Kids learn words from others, either in real life. Or in the game, and they'll mirror them. ROBLOX is good about warning players to not swear, but again. Kids attempt to cheat the system, using words like: (Excuse my profanity) "Fk u", which is derived from "Fuck you", "Sht" for "Shit". And so on and forth.
While ROBLOX does provide the filter to prevent them from being visible to other players, I believe it is in need of more phrases. For the role-playing games, yes. They're more difficult to get rid of, but I don't think they're the main problem.

3, Violence: As a Parent, your last expectation from a "Kids" game is to see gross and graphic violence, those sorts of actions are more fit for an "Adult" game. But some of the games on ROBLOX have Violence, whether by Guns, Bombs, Swords, etc. It includes some very violent games (Albeit not as an exact copy) such as "Yandere Simulator", "Call of Duty", "Grand Theft Auto", (Rights reserved to their respective holders) "Call of Duty" and "Grand Theft Auto" are both Mature rated games by the ESRB (Entertainment Software Rating Board) [ESRB.org]

Done with Cons? Let's move onto some of the Pros;

1, Education: ROBLOX strives on "Powering Imagination™" this goes on to allowing all players to create their own Games. Models and Scripts, using their proprietary studio program; (Roblox Studio) Using the studio, it allows players to create 3D worlds out of anything they could ever imagine. They let players create functions using the scripting engine built into the program (Lua) easy to learn and understand. They also let players make their own shirts, T-Shirts and pants. (However, to sell them for in-game currency, you have you purchase any of their Builders Club memberships, and it remains for the duration of the membership) This teaches them how to construct objects in a 3D space, empowers them to learn basic programming code. And allows them to show off their creativity in all aspects.

2, Ability to make Friends: ROBLOX provides a platform for making friends with similar interests, by joining a "Group" you can find players with interests like yours, they empower friendship. Giving the ability to learn how to communicate with others using their Private-Messaging system (PM)

3, Groups: Mentioned in 2, there is a multitude of Groups, thousands if I'm not mistaken, Kids can find groups that fit their interests, whether it be to work in a Pizza Place, going around the galaxy in a star-ship, or traveling through space and time. There's bound to be a group that fits your child's interests.

If your Child is interested, and the Parent allows, ROBLOX is a great place to find other kids who have the same interests as your Child, teach how to construct places in 3D, or learn how to program.

PARENTS: While I hope that all goes well, and nobody attempts to threaten you or your Child. Nobody is always keen to follow the rules, I suggest to watch your Child's actions, especially when they talk to other members online.

column6: Roblox is a fun browser based game that is completely free to play and almost all the games are free.  All games  are player made, which means that members of roblox created them. Anyone can create a game.  There are some things though that parents need to know. Roblox does have a moderation system. They try to keep people from swearing, but sometimes it still comes through. If there is innapropriate content in a user's message, it is usually changed to #'s or [Content Deleted]. But people can sometimes get around that by putting extra letters into it. Another precaution roblox takes is by putting users on the whitelist and the blacklist. Users under 13 are put on the whitelist, which means that any word not on the whitelist will appear as #'s to them and any others playing. Users 13 and older are put on the blacklist, which means any word they say that is on the blacklist is replaced by #'s for them and any others. There are also people who try and steal other users accounts. If you are going to let your child play roblox, make sure to tell them not to give any account information away. There is some violence in some player created roblox games, but because of how roblox is designed, it isn't as graphic as some games. There is also Builders Club, which is a paid option that lets you have better stuff. Some people require you to have Builders Club to play their game. Those games are actually not as fun as some of the free games. Some of these things seem negative, but roblox can encourage players to learn how to create games and how to script and code. The games can be quite fun. There are some people I noticed who were lying about some of the things in roblox. Front page games never have any innapropriate content in them because roblox moderation would delete them immediately if they did.
