There is a high chance that someone will confiscate your account, however, there is a possibility that they weren't lying however this is highly unlikely.
2. Blocking/muting- If someone is saying bad things to you, you can block them by going to the player list (in the top right), clicking the username of the rude person, and then clicking the rectangle that says "Block". This will make all the chat that the blocked person says be invisible forever, but can be undone. You could also make this happen by doing "/mute {player}". If you use the mute version, then they won't be permanently muted, as they can rejoin the server and they will regain ability to say things to you.
3. Robux:
Robux is the ingame currency that allows you to buy gamepasses, which allow you to do extra things inside of games or customise your avatar -your appearance-if you do not have a secure password on your credit card, then there is a high risk of your child/ you (lucky for you) to obtain Robux using the parent's/ your money. If this happens, don't blame Roblox, just blame yourself, as you'd be the stupid one for  having a password that even a child can infer.
4.  Limitations                                                                                                                         
  If you are not comfortable with your child swearing and you don't want them to ever swear on roblox, you can make the date of birth on the roblox account the highest possible, and they will have strict limitations.  EG: 31/08/19. Even numbers are censored. This can be EXTREMLEY annoying at times, however, this prevents people from saying their age.

5. Getting a job
If your child likes video games and you say that they'll never get a job from video games, I'm here to prove you wrong. In 2018 alone, Roblox gave away about 80 Million Dollars worldwide to Roblox developers. If you didn't know, a Roblox developer is someone who makes games on Roblox, they can build things and script things. Overall, I think this game is good for children ages 4 and above. You just need to be cautious when playing the game for anything questionable.

column5: Hear me out here before you think this is a bad review because of the star rating
column6:
If you are a parent who does not want to expose your child to the "bad" parts of the world, be my guest. You do not have to let your child play. Unfortunately you cannot delete accounts but you can probably block ROBLOX from the computer if you have that type of software. But if you want to "delete" the account you can give out your child's password in the "About" section of the settings so that other players might take it(also make sure that they don't have the e-mail in so they could probably take over the account completely).
Yep it sounds cruel, but that's probably the easiest way to get your child's account "deleted". Getting banned is pretty hard in this 'game' now that they don't have forums.

Now for the actual review, is there sexual acts? Yep and it's probably on practically every online game ever. Anyway, they used to be quite common on MeepCity (a 'game' on ROBLOX--I'll explain this later if you haven't caught my drift by the end of this paragraph) and even I have witnessed them. However, the 'creator' of MeepCity got rid of the actions allowing this and also made sure that you couldn't name parties anymore (since those were the main problems in the game causing sexual acts).

Now if you're confused, ROBLOX is not a game. It is a platform, if you will, so that your kids can play games and make them if they know how to code, model, and animate their models, otherwise I highly doubt they'll be able to make anything that could rise in the ranks of ROBLOX's games. MeepCity is one of the more popular games in ROBLOX. If you have seen Club Penguin and Toontown, both from Disney ironically, then that is pretty much Meep City.  Now that game is better but it probably still has online daters. (The majority of online dating, however, is simply harmless roleplaying, but some of it is malicious and therefore it should be avoided.)

There are lots of games with violence and death, such as Jailbreak ( has the guns and such), Phantom Forces (it has lots of guns and stuff), Murder Mystery 2, Counter Blox Roblox Offensive, and Assassin! (which is, at the moment, called [COMP] Assassin! but anything in brackets tend to be the game talking about its newest update) However, these are only to name a few popular ones. There is death in almost every ROBLOX game where 'resetting' ('killing' your character so they return back to spawn point) is not disabled. The death is very cartoony and simple, your character just 'falls' down and has their limbs and head detached from the torso. (there is no blood in that animation, just see it for yourself, it looks rather funny in fact) NOTE that in some games the death animation is altered, so it may look more realistic or the death animation doesn't exist at all, you might just vanish. For example, in Murder Mystery 2 if I remember clearly when you are hit by a knife you will fall down like a real death, but I don't think there's any blood. However, in other games it may look like that but HAVE blood, though it tends to be cartoony blood (but still red and vaguely resembling blood). Before you think this is all bad, there are many child friendly games (many being roleplaying games where you interact with other players with your own made up character as if it was a book like the RPG board games if you will) like Wolves' Life. However players in those games may make it potentially slightly violent.

One thing to mention, 'swear' words (or replacement words for swear words) may come out. However, I remember one instance where the chat filter allowed a certain cuss word to go through. This isn't entirely ROBLOX's fault, however, because ROBLOX uses a sort of 'advanced' filter called CommunitySift for those 12 and under, while it uses their own filter for those 13 and up I believe. So in reality, it was CommunitySift's fault cursing was allowed to go through.

There is lots of consumerism in this one, but it is never required. You can buy 'robux' (NOT 'robucks') OR Builders Club for your child so they can buy gamepasses, clothing, make their own groups if they have Builders Club, or donate to groups or other players if they have Builders Club. (Builders club is most likely required in order to make sure scamming does not take place.) You can teach your kid money management in this game or management of 'groups'. There are many military/army, airplane, hotel, and other business groups which have ranks. These groups are like 'jobs', where your child can work and get promoted. (They have to go to the groups 'game' in order to 'work', and many of these groups have a 'training' stage for you to get a hold of what you're doing before you actually get the job and robux) In my opinion these groups give good messages about working for what you want.

Also here are some games I recommend avoiding:
0  Life in Paradise--OD'ing
0   Any 'Adopt a Baby' or 'Make a Family' or any titles of that sort  games--there is OD'ing (BUT "Adopt Me!" is okay because you just adopt a kid and run around trying to make sure their stats are filled. People don't really OD here because there is not much time to talk or roleplay)
0  Boys and Girls Club (Potential Sex and OD'ing, trust me I went here once to troll and it ended up with a girl telling me to take off my clothes by a bed in that game. Then I told her I was a girl since I was dressed as a boy (remember I was trolling or if you don't know what trolling is think of pranks) and she instantly left the server :'D)

People can be mean in any game as long as it has chatting. Unfortunately that is just the world we live in now but rude people aren't too common actually unless you are in a game that involves fighting, then they may be common. OR if you are in one of the games I have mentioned people may be rude to you if you don't have 'ROBUX' clothing)

I recommend this game for mature children 9 and up.  If you noticed the beginning of this review, I said it was hard to get banned. This is because moderators are probably more busy making sure games have appropriate content instead of the players themselves being appropriate. If you want a more moderated 'game', this is not the game for you.

This game has gotten far more kid-friendly (specifically little kids).  There is a chat filter in the game, and if you are over protective, you can enable something that disables your kid from chatting and in-game chat will become invisible. The community has improved and your kid will probably improve social skills by playing this game (in moderation of course). Yes, a lot of the popular games have violence, but im sure your kid already knows all of the violent stuff in these games, and if you dont want your kid playing these games, there is a plethora of games that aren't violent AT ALL. 

ROBLOX isn't just about playing games, there are lots of features that can benefit your kid dramatically. I can't even stress how much your kid can learn from these features. Parents should know that there a multitude of games available to be played that range from simple building, to fast paced combat. Families can easily predict the safety of the game by simply looking at the title, as hotspots of people giving out their personal information are typically titled 'dance club' or 'adopt a kid'. If a child steers clear of games like that, their experience should be safe. ROBLOX is somewhat of a pay to win, with the ROBLOX corporation offering paid memberships that give you more space for groups, no ads (however player created ads are shown), and the in game currency 'ROBUX'. Since the removal of 'TIX' a currency that was free for all, all purchases on ROBLOX are limited to 'ROBUX'. A player without membership can earn robux through selling virtual items for their games, however achieving profits can be hard without 'ROBUX'. ROBLOX does have a great community, with groups that will for sure fit your child's interests. Groups are created by players and range from fan clubs and re-enactment groups to war groups. Parents should be aware of the privacy settings ROBLOX has. If a parent wishes to have their child blocked from all contact from strangers, they may do so. ROBLOX does however have numerous scammers which, should parents choose to buy membership or 'ROBUX' may result in their accounts being stolen. Despite popular belief there is no free 'ROBUX'. ROBLOX is a great game with a mostly great community, but parents still should teach their children about online safety and the risks of playing and chatting with strangers.

ROBLOX can suggest games for you to play based on what you've already played. If you like a game, give it a thumbs up. If you don't, give it a thumbs down.

Nowadays, when you sign up for ROBLOX, based on your gender you are automatically given a terrible looking lego-like figure. Please remove this immediately. Most users discriminate against it and it is only ever used ironically. There are a few other free things you can get from the catalog that will make you fit in better.

Sometimes, users will swear on ROBLOX. They only do this because of the poor hashtag sensor system. If we all report the swearing people, we can prevent swearing altogether. Besides, they're all probably spoiled 6-year-olds who play Call of Duty, anyways.

Be warned that admin reports are poor. If you report a user, you better have a good, well-thought out reason that anybody can understand, or you yourself will be misunderstood, and banned for a couple of weeks.

IF YOU ARE SENSITIVE, I suggest you stay away from battle games like "Sword Fight on the Heights" if you aren't experienced with using a sword on ROBLOX.

PLEASE BE AWARE, ABOUT BATTLE GAMES, I think they're only accepted because all players re-appear at a checkpoint if they die. There is NO blood in battle games; the only thing that happens is the player's arms and head fall off and the body disappears, similar to in the LEGO video games.

The Forums are a pretty good way to socialize in the ROBLOX community. I recommend staying away from "Off Topic" and "All Things ROBLOX". Off Topic is full of "Trolls", and All Things ROBLOX is almost never on topic.

Be warned that the site's premium membership, "Builder's Club", is overly advertised. There are many features that require Builder's Club, such as having more than one ROBLOX place of your own open at a time, creating custom clothes, etc. Builder's Club isn't cheap, either. Before you discriminate against this, how much money do YOU think it cost to run a website with THOUSANDS of users who log in every day? If you're worried about your kid doing bad things or playing bad games or wondering if they're getting their feelings hurt, or whatever you're wondering, just make your own account and follow them around secretly.

In closing, if you make a free account, choose your friends wisely, play games with caution, and report the bad stuff with good reasoning, I believe anyone can have a safe, fun experience on ROBLOX.

column5: Watch out for predators and people looking for Roblox boyfriends - and look out for those Robux, too
column6:
I know Roblox can be an unsafe environment for younger children, but in my experience I've had relatively minor (but still alarming) issues. It honestly depends on which server you play in (which game you choose). For example, there have been no issues on 'Feather Family' (a bird roleplay game, where you play as a bird and interact with other players to make a story), but both of the incidents I've experienced have been on 'Brookhaven' (an open human roleplay server). Set in a small town with upper-class vibes, players can choose a job (from SWAT team to YouTuber), name their in-game customizable avatar, and acquire a house or apartment. The incidents in question are as follows: a player presenting as male offered to be my bodyguard (after several occurrences of children breaking into my house) and so I gave him roommate permissions (he could unlock the door to my house and possibly also change other house-related settings). He disappeared while I went on a wild goose chase to find one of the kids who broke into my house, and upon finding the offender, I tried to locate my 'bodyguard'. When I finally did, just up the road, he pulled out a gun and told me he was going to (unalive) me. This, of course, caught me off guard and I left the game without saying anything. It was hard to tell if he was joking, or if it was just part of the roleplay. It's a shock that, while messages like "I told you" get blocked, the words "I'm going to kill you" still get through. There are some major issues with this system. The second incident was on the same server. My roleplay character presented as male this time, and I posted on a billboard that I was looking for a roommate. Almost immediately, I got a response from a player presenting as female. She greeted me with a "hey 😏" and once she had given me roommate permissions to her house, she immediately asked whether or not I had a "girl" (resulting in me logging off immediately again). I think the big problem with these games is that a lot of kids and possibly teenagers are looking for "Roblox girlfriends" or "Roblox boyfriends", which can make them easy prey for predators. Make sure you monitor your child, and I'd recommend that they stay away from Brookhaven. ///////

Edit: As a side note, watch out for Robux purchases and processes (the in-game currency paid for by real money). My brother is nine and constantly wants to buy more Robux, as in a majority of the games he plays on Roblox have things to be purchased built in. Look out for that.

Edit 2: Look out for servers where players can "donate" Robux to each other. It seems as if most people on these servers are trying to scam people, or simply spam the chat with repetitive, cookie-cutter phrases to encourage others to donate to them. One player's "stand" was obviously hacked to me, but it might not have been as obvious to young children. When I clicked on an item that stated its cost as five Robux, I was confused as to why it showed the balance on my account went way down if I chose to purchase said item. ("Your balance after this purchase will be 56 Robux.") Then I realized that, even though it said I'd be paying five, the mediator screen showed I'd have to pay 299 Robux! There were several other things wrong with that player's stand, but I'll leave it at that. I reported them and pointed out their scam to them in chat. Additionally, their avatar looked like a fully-grown man with no idea of what teenage girls like to put on their Roblox figures put together what he thought was the most "attractive" outfit. //////

Edit 2 (cont'd): There are also many issues with the moderation system. Words like "ass" and "hell" come through, but the words "bro" and "ok" get censored. There have been several occasions where someone spams the chat with potty language or repetitive sentences. Please monitor your child while using this app/game if you would not like them to be exposed to such occurrences.

column6: Roblox is a fun game where you play other people’s games and you can become friends with people and earn followers around the world. Building a game yourself isn’t to hard either. Although good messages with teamwork and friendship, some games can contain violence. One game, “Murder Mystery 2”, when you are murdered you can hear a stabbing sound, but the screen just goes black. The game ends when the murderer kills everyone, the murderer leaves the game, or the sheriff/hero shoots the murderer (again, the shooting is not graphic, the murderer just falls to the ground with no blood, just a gunshot sound effect). Another game called “Flee the Facility” is based on the violent game “Dead by Daylight”, where a beast comes and tries to capture players into a frozen cubicle and freeze you to death. In order to escape, you must hack all computers and exit through the door. If you fail to hack, the beast will see where you are. The game ends when everyone is frozen, the beast leaves the server, or when everyone escaped. This is not as graphic as “Dead by daylight”, but has a similar vibe and tone and can get pretty intense.  Other games, such as “Piggy” and “Bacon” are similar, with the exception of death cries (usually male). “Arsenal” is similar to “war” games such as “Call of Duty”. You are placed in a team and you have to defeat the other team by shooting them. Some guns in the game are real guns, such as AK-47s, pistols and revolvers, Uzis, Machine Guns, etc. Again, not as violent as COD but pretty intense with shooting sounds. “Jailbreak” and “Mad City” are similar to “GTA”. You rob banks and other artifacts and bring them back to base to earn money. You can shoot other people from another team with different guns. You can play as the criminal or cop in “Jailbreak”, and you can play as criminal, hero, or cop in “Mad City”. Similar to GTA, but not as violent and without language and sex. When you die (such as falling or getting killed in the game) or reset, you either get a screen with the border line briefly glowing red (meaning you died) or your body parts such as limbs, heads, arms , legs get dismembered and fall apart like a toy (not graphic). Kids can actually purchase a currency in the game called “Robux” from their parents’ account, so be aware of that. Kids ages 12 and under will have safe games with no graphic content. Teens 13 and up are more exposed to more violent games. You can never be sure of this, because some games can still be violent without Roblox knowing that it is. Both age ranges have  profane language blocked as hashtags (#), but, again, you can never be sure of that. I waited until I was 13 to compare the game when I was a kid and when I was a teen. Not much of the games are different, and basically the account information just updated. So even though there is a safe option for kids 12 and under, it is still most safe for kids 13 and up to play just because you can never know what explicit material the game may contain and that more and more games are being made and Roblox can’t always check and play them to arrange it for kids or for teens. So according to video game ratings in North America here, ESRB has rated it Everyone 10+. This is a little bit inaccurate, due to the ESRB only reviewing some samples of the games selected. But if your child is 10 or older and you think they are mature enough, then that is ok with me. IOS is more careful, with rating it 12+, which I personally think is more accurate. I suggest looking at the parents guide at IMDb for more: https://m.imdb.com/title/tt6667676/parentalguide?ref_=m_ttpg_crt

column6:
This is one of the most worldwide known games "for kids". There is so much good content to play on it but here I am going to be talking about all of the bad side.

CHAT MODERATION
Roblox is infamous for their flawed automated chat moderation. Some potentially inappropriate words or sentences that may contain personal information may be put into hashtags however it is very easy to work around this system.

BUILDING
Also, if you think this game is for creating, turn back right now. If I were to guess, 99.99% of users on Roblox play games rather than create them. 

However, there are some games that encourage creating, such as 'Sandbox' (however this game is now relatively unpopular and unknown), 'Skyblox' (a bit of a Minecraft rip) and 'Adopt Me' (this includes a house customization feature but I would not recommend this game if you are to stop reading)

IN-APP PURCHASES
Roblox is also packed with in-app purchases stuffed in your face. To be considered 'cool' children will usually spend real money to obtain Robux and buy clothing, or Gamepasses which allow you to have an ingame advantage in a select game.

Adopt Me, and any game that has 'Simulator' in the name is known for in-app purchases being slapped all over the screen.

RO-GANGSTERS
Continuing on from being 'cool', there is a player stereotype known as the 'Ro-Gangster'. These people often bypass the chat filter with swearing, bully/threaten others, use bypassed/inappropriate audios, songs and decals, ONLINE DATE and perform sexual acts by abusing emotes. They also may tell you to 'mic up' on Discord where they can say and post anything but a lot of these users are all bark and no bite. Soo if your child or you has/have Discord, just saying, stay safe on there

Playing any game that isn't on the very top of the list on the Games page will have a pretty good chance of encountering somebody that fits this description.

BUDGETING
A very large majority of clothing is botted and stolen. All of the clothing on the front page catalog is botted.

I believe that Robux may be a good opportunity to teach your child to budget. A good majority of legitimate clothing costs 5 to 15 robux, you should never spend more than that, and be picky with what you spend on accessories!

There is also a market of 'Limited Accessories' that have changing prices and are only owned by a set amount of players...moving onto scamming.

SCAMS
Scamming is a very large issue. Not so much in Limited Accessory trading but in bots or stolen accounts that will encourage players to visit phishing links or scam games. That link or scam game will then try to trick the user into putting their username and password in.

If you were to fall victim to one of these scams, there is a good chance that your account was not taken and you can still login, but your account has been used to paste the same message everywhere. These scams target bigger fish, aka users with premium and a decent amount of robux.

Any games with a trading system, Adopt Me, Royale High and Bubble Gum Simulator in particular, are also full of children trying to scam eachother. Make sure you only ever use the trading system to trade, and only trade NORMALLY. I'm not going to list every scam ever but if you get scammed, it can be a valuable lesson. Lol

General safety advice as well, don't visit any sketchy out of Roblox link.

VIOLENCE
Violence, surprisingly there is not too much violence, with it being more cracked down on than other things... Any games with violence are quickly held for review and you are unable to play until the developer removes it. Except for a couple of games below:

GAMES TO WATCH OUT FOR:

Meep-City
The dead version of Adopt Me, was once very popular, now there are parties hosted ingame that have many 'Ro-Gangster' like players, who will bypass the chat, play inappropriate audios/songs, have single/'uncuffed' or taken/'cuffed' in their character description, and perform many sexual acts and abuse the house editing system (placing a pole and pole dancing, and doing 'the deed' by abusing the sleeping emote)

Dollhouse Roleplay
Similar problems to above. Full of Ro-Gangsters, playing loud inappropriate audios and songs. Whatever bad audio you think exists, trust me, it is played and bypassed in this game.

The Streets and Da Hood
Games full of Ro-Gangsters, doing all of the behaviors listed before as well as using a spray can to use bypassed decals (of highly inappropriate things) and also encourage 'tea-bagging' (search that up yourself.......) and with the main objective of these games being to collect money and chase down and kill other players.
There are other alternatives with objectives of a similar nature (Arsenal, Phantom Forces) however the community and overall vibe is much better and the objective is more focused on improving at shooting and unlocking new cosmetics.

Club Iris(or any other club game for that matter)
All the cons of Dollhouse roleplay.

De Pride Isle Sanatorium
Disguised as a LGBTQ+ community, gives twisted views on LGBTQ+, race, gender, ideal body type. Infamous for having surgeries and drugs ingame presented as 'Holy Water' and 'Plastic Surgery'. Older versions of the game also had CANNABALISM ingame and Roblox has taken this game down only for it to keep coming back. The owner's account is also on their last strike, they are known for being racist, transphobic, homophobic,,,,
Very toxic community, do not associate. Also don't go near any Barbie lookalikes in this game. The barbie-lookalike are also found in fashion runway games and you should not play any of these except Boho Salon, Fashion Famous and Roblox's Top Model, which are safe fashion show games.

There you have it, the bad side of Roblox in a nutshell. In conclusion, it is way too hard to moderate what your child is seeing or doing, instead, play with them or don't let them play at all. Fun game but very dangerous unsupervised..imagine writing hundreds of words on it

column5: It used to be better, honest.
column6:
I started playing Roblox as a guest in December 2008 and I created an account a few months after. My first game was 'Work at a Pizza Place' (which is, surprisingly, still popular) and I enjoyed it very much. Games back then were creative and one could still have a good time even if a 'deleter' (a term applied to griefers (people who ruin others' experiences) who delete someone's work) intruded. The community back then was conventional and if one swore or broke the rules, punishment was acceptable and just.

In my opinion, the game is more about fun than learning. With that being said, however, I have heard of users using this website and learning how to 'script' and becoming indie game developers themselves. Aside from that field of learning, Roblox is better to learn how to make friends.

As a player who has played for this amount of time, I am heartbroken to see what the game has become. Scamming and spam is comparable to what it was before, however it is still an issue. In many games now, inappropriate language and uncouth behaviour runs rampant. I would advise anyone not seeking to experience bad language to avoid games which are inherently designed for communicating and not to achieve something (ie games which are like 'clubs', 'hangouts', 'high schools', etc).

In one recent game of mine, I walked into an area in a club wearing an outfit that is dated now, due to the fact that it was made in 2009 and immediately I was insulted with very offensive racial slurs (despite not being the race whereof they insulted). I end up reporting at least five times a day; not for minor infractions but for extremely harsh language.

The game is also different now due to the fact that there is an increasing wealth gap that can isolate 'non-members' from 'members'. For example, in order to purchase an item that costs '100 Robux' (Robux being a form of in-game currency), members of the highest subscription only need to wait 2 days. Members of the middle subscription need to wait 3 and members of the lowest subscription need to wait 7 days. A non-member, however, provided that they do not purchase Robux, would have to log in once each day (this may be inaccurate because I have not looked at the fluctuations for some time now) for at least (it is more, but I do not know exactly) 1000 days (almost 3 years). This is because 10 TIX = 1 Robux.  This huge gap between about 3 years and 1 day of waiting results in a caste system whereby non-members can only afford basic items.

Roblox has been effective at combating hacking, however it happens a lot in very old places because they can be exploited easily. The worst hacks I have seen have involved extremely adult content, however this last happened a year ago if not more. I have noticed a surge in online dating (often shortened to 'ODing' - sometimes erroneously referred to as 'OD'ing' - to avoid a ban). 

Spam messages from female account bots with usernames such as "jaimeaustin481" will provide a link within their messages, which will lead to one's account being compromised if one should follow the link.

There is not much violence, however there are games which involve shooting and killing zombies, for example. This is less than what it was years ago, when some games would incorporate 'blood' and hackers would hack in a 'slit throat', which has been patched.

Overall, I would say that the game has too much swearing and consumerism and that it is quite easy to lose one's account should one click a bad link sent to them by a bot.

column6:
After joining this game back in 2010 a lot has changed over the years. When I joined, the developers and admin team actually enforced rules, people were creative with their game ideas, and the community wasn't as toxic as it is today. Now in 2018, this game has become unplayable and not enjoyable. I understand that over the years Roblox had become bigger and had to be more kid friendly which is fine. But instead of trying to make games and express creativity, this game has become a social media site with excessive amounts of toxicity. Over the years, Roblox has tried to fix their issues with implementing updates that did nothing but drive away the veteran players such as myself. For example, they implemented a chat filtering system to cut back on the amount of swearing which is good, but the filtering system got so bad that I can't even say numbers or specific words that have nothing to do with a bad context. But even before the filter, the admin team would kick and enforce rules to those who even said an abbreviation or derivative of a swear word. 

Over my experience, I have composed a list of what not to do in this game due to safety issues.

1. Do not spend money or buy builder's club memberships. If you buy these with a credit card, you will become a big target for hackers who will steal your information. 

2. Do not give out any personal information such as age, location, or anything along those lines. Its okay to have friends, but make sure they are only your friends on Roblox and not in real life unless you personally know them. 

3. Make sure you do not give out passwords to people since they will go to your account and take it over, spend your money on your credit cards, and whatever else they feel like doing. 

Bullying Concerns: Even though there is bullying going on in the real world and online, there is a button called "block a player" or something along those lines which will block a player from communicating to you, and I believe there is an in-game mute button to mute players.  Those above a few ways to limit or prevent bullying. 

Consumerism: This game before was a favorite for many since there was an opportunity to play the game and buy all the cool stuff for free. Each day you logged in, you would get tickets which could be converted into Robux or used to buy things such as in-game clothing, hats, gear, and other interesting things. This game has always been free, but if you want to look cool or look anything like they do in the commercials, you need to spend money. The prices for these extra things are not cheap either and will burn holes through your pockets. For example, there is a pirate hat that is about 2,000 Robux, which in USD is around $25. Builder's Club Membership is nice, but will make you a big target for hackers. There are 3 levels of Builder's Club and each will give you more benefits than the other, but for more money. This link is for each level and it's benefits. https://www.roblox.com/premium/membership?ctx=leftnav
A cool feature to this game is the limited items market and trading. It works like the economy where you need money to start up your business and a risk/benefit factor. Then you can trade and sell items to make profits, but you need builders club and you will need Robux to start which is a double whammy. If you are successful, you will probably never have to spend money on this game since some of the items are worth $1,000s in real life.

Game-Creating: This game is also nice because you can make your own games, but if they get popular you can make money with a Developer Exchange Program where you can make good money, but it will take a lot of hard work. Once again, you would need Builder's Club to participate in that program. https://www.roblox.com/develop/developer-exchange
This link will show you requirements and other things having to do with the Developer Exchange. They are really stupid in my opinion. 

Online-Dating Issues: Online Dating on Roblox has always been an issue around the 2011-2012 time period and is still going strong to this day. Roblox may become a hotspot for sexual predators if it hasn't already since this game is becoming huge and popular. The problem is that kids and teens will try to go out with someone they don't know. They will never know who that person is until they meet them on the street, and after you meet them, you are screwed. Word of advice, don't do it, and if someone tries to pressure you, then you need to block them and/or leave the game and go to a different server. 

Overall Summary: This game isn't the game it used to be and gets a ton of hate due to its current state unfortunately. This game back in 2011ish and before was great since it was a smaller community and it didn't have so much toxicity even though its always been around. Consumerism has taken a toll on the community and it seems that little to none care about the community anymore. The updates Roblox comes out with are usually for the worst instead of the best. Online-Dating is still a huge issue that many seem to either care or not care about. 

Thank you for reading this!

column6:
I've played the game on and off for about 6 years. There's a few things you need to know about this game;

- The game is HEAVILY monetized. Player-created clothing items are fairly expensive (one shirt or pair of pants taking 10 days (at best) to save up for), but fear not - you can either purchase in-game currency straight out, or subscribe to a monthly Builder's Club. The prices aren't outrageous at first glance, but note that in-game currency will not last as long as you think it will.

Users can create their own groups for their friends to join - but, again, not for free.  At the time of writing this, if your child wanted to create his own group for 100 Robux (the in-game currency) WITHOUT paying real money, it would take 136 days of saving up. Yikes.

Aside from groups, ROBLOX features a 'Front Page' of games that other users have made and are currently playing, sorted into categories like the most popular games on the site, the top games that require in-game currency to enter, and the top games that require a subscription to the Builder's Club. There are way too many examples of in-game items or features being massively expensive to list - the site is mostly just a cash grab.

As for your child being able to create his own games, he'll use either the in-game tools - which are fairly simple - or user-made tools. They will also be much better off with an at least basic understanding of the programming language Lua. Note that the game does not give many advanced tutorials with this - there are tutorials, though, but me and my friends found these fairly difficult to follow - your mileage may vary - and the few in-depth tutorials are created by users who themselves have a good understanding of the language. The catch? At the time of writing, all of these tutorial games cost in-game currency. Yep.

Don't worry, though, users can join groups for free - though you're limited to being in 5 without paying real cash - and play most games for free. Do note that users can create 'game passes' for their games, which require a decent amount of in game currency.

Users can also browse the forums - though, if your child is under 18, make sure they stay far, FAR away from them. The forums seem to be poorly moderated, with offensive messages being posted practically every few minutes. Vulgar language or direct personal attacks on other users (eg. "You're autistic". Yes, forumers do use that term.) are common and users will usually get away with this.

Other forum content includes sexist, racist or otherwise offensive posts, posting of users' IP addresses (which can be used to maliciously attack other users, like in the case of DoSing (just google it)), and links to nude pictures of users are frequently found on the forums.

The front page of games isn't all clean, either. Sometimes, exceptionally inappropriate games make it to the front page for any and all users to see (including sexual content). ROBLOX does moderate these, however, their response time is lacking. By the time the place would be deleted and the creator banned from the site, thousands of users would have already visited it.

This is not to mention ROBLOX's blatantly broken moderation system. Games on the front page frequently feature online dating situations (called 'ODing' by users), even though ODing is forbidden by ROBLOX. While personal attacks against other users are also forbidden, the forums and in-game chat are riddled with comments from 'autistic' to 'fking tard' to 'pls drink clorox'. While the game does feature a 'Report Abuse' option both in game and on other user content, any punishment is rare.

It's also worth mentioning that users can create their own clothing - if they're subscribed to Builder's Club - and sell it to make money in game. Unfortunately, it is extremely easy to download a user's clothing and upload it yourself, either to get it yourself for free or to sell it at a profit to other users. ROBLOX has, for YEARS, known about this issue, and it's not only frequent, but ROBLOX doesn't even have a rule against it.

Speaking of moderation, the ROBLOX moderation system features an 'appeal' system, where users can ask that their bans from the site be lifted. On paper, this would prevent users from being wrongfully banned. Unfortunately, ROBLOX support will likely not respond before the ban has already run out.

As for violence on the site, games frequently feature it. First- or third-person shooters are common on the site, with user places resembling the likes of Halo, Call of Duty or Grand Theft Auto (with violence to match).

In conclusion, the games are violent, the forums are a cesspool of hate and inappropriate content, and the whole site is filled to the brim with microtransactions. Take a good look before letting your kids play.

this is such a good book. it reminds me of the critically acclaimed series known as jojo's bizarre adventure. The first part, Phantom Blood, is set in Liverpool, England in 1880 and follows the adventures of a young man named Jonathan Joestar, known as JoJo, living on his wealthy father George's estate. George takes in a homeless boy, Dio Brando who bullies the innocent Jonathan, plotting to become the sole heir to the Joestar fortune. However, his attempts are thwarted and he resorts to using an ancient Stone Mask which transforms him into a vampire with his sights now set on world domination. Jonathan, with Italian Hamon master Will A. Zeppeli and former street thug Robert E.O. Speedwagon at his side, uses his newly found affinity for Hamon to stop Dio who appears to be killed and Jonathan passes away. However Jonathan's pregnant wife, Erina gives birth to a son, continuing the Joestar name.

The second part, Battle Tendency, takes place fifty years later in 1938 as Jonathan's grandson, Joseph Joestar. He hears of Speedwagon's apparent death during an excavation, and when he investigates, he becomes entangled with the revival of the Pillar Men, ancient humanoids of impossible power who are tied to the creation of the Stone Mask. Joseph ultimately teams up with Caesar Zeppeli, Will's grandson, and Caesar's teacher Lisa Lisa, who is linked to Joseph. They try to stop the Pillar Men led by Kars and Esidisi from obtaining a mystical artifact in Lisa Lisa's possession that will grant them complete immortality and bring about the end of the world. With the help of his friends and allies, Joseph eventually masters Hamon and beats the Pillar Men.
in the thrilling third part of the series, Set in 1987, the series follows Jotaro Kujo and his comrades who have developed mysterious powers known as Stands. Jotaro, his grandfather Joseph Joestar and their allies, travel to Egypt in search of the evil and immortal vampire Dio Brando, now known solely as "DIO" to save Jotaro's mother Holly, whose Stand has awakened and threatens to consume her in 50 days. Meanwhile, DIO has commissioned a number of assassins with various types of deadly Stands to destroy them before they can reach him..
however in the fourth part, Set in 1999, 11 years after the events of Stardust Crusaders, Jotaro Kujo tracks down Josuke Higashikata, the illegitimate son of Joseph Joestar, to help him find a magical bow and arrow which grants people Stand powers. Along the way, Josuke and his friends discover that a Stand-using serial killer is on the loose in their hometown of Morioh and they set out to stop him.
finally in the last animated part (as of 2019) Set in 2001, two years after the events of Diamond is Unbreakable, Koichi Hirose is sent to Italy and tasked by Jotaro Kujo to search for Giorno Giovanna, an aspiring mafia gangster who is a son of Dio Brando. But as Dio possessed the body of Jonathan Joestar at time of his conception, Giorno is technically a Joestar and takes more after them than the father he never knew. The series follows Giorno as he joins the mafia organization Passione, moving up through its ranks with the intention of becoming its boss to improve life in Italy.

Roblox is a sandbox game that allows for one to create anything that one would imagine.  With its rise in popularity, I decided to download and play the game for myself.  I immediately regretted this decision and I had the sudden urge to throw myself off Mount Everest.  Yeah, it was that bad, and let me explain why:

The controls are a nightmare, movement is awkward, camera controls belong to the Nintendo 64 (a comparison to how outdated these controls are), and the animations are stiff and poorly designed.  Mini games vary in quality, as the creators can have inappropriate concepts within the game (from sex, to swearing, to drinking, to bad influences, etc.).

Despite my comments from the previous section (and despite what FamilyZone has to say about this game, link to their review: https://www.familyzone.com/blog/roblox-parents-review), there are more dangerous games out there.  If this came out prior to Night Trap (the game that created the ESRB ratings in 1992), I would doubt that this game would cause outrage and force a rating system that would keep dangerous games away from children.  There are other games with more violence and explicit content than Roblox (which is, by the way, its only redeemable quality).

One problem I had when making this review was what age group should be playing this game.  My answer: play Mario Odyssey when that comes out.  Recently, I've noticed a lot of children on games they shouldn't have.  Kids playing Call of Duty, Halo, Fallout, and even games that seem innocent like Roblox.  Parents ought to be more careful when a game has voice chat or any form of in-game chat, as I have received rude messages, death threats, sexually explicit phrases, etc.  Even if a game has a system that could censor swears, people can find a way to surpass such systems.

Overall, I believe that Roblox is the poor man's Minecraft.  Minecraft is also a sandbox game, but with better controls, better design, and a better community (which is really saying something because the Minecraft community is terrible).  If your child is older than 13 and has a Steam account (or you're willing to get one for free), I would recommend Terraria, another sandbox game that has easily the greatest community out of the three and the most bang for your buck.
